objective: Close review R3 by retaining event behavior while replacing the Python 3.11-only UTC import and proving compatibility on the local Python 3.10 and 3.11 runtimes.
deliverable: event_log.py, focused tests, and a structured worker receipt.
read_scope: fixtures/adaptive-task-orchestrator-write-dag/tests/ and tools/ (read-only except declared new files)
write_scope: Unique automatically cleaned unittest TemporaryDirectory paths outside the project

authoritative_facts: Each task revision owns exactly one event stream; no concurrent shared append is permitted.
A valid span contains exactly one started then one finished event for one task/revision/span identity.
Current timestamps are comparable only on this local host and do not support cross-machine claims.
Review R3 proved datetime.UTC fails to import on local Python 3.10.0 while py -3 Python 3.11.9 passes.
accepted_upstream_results: V3-T3@1 was accepted before V3-T6@2 found R3; preserve revision 1 evidence and repair through revision 2.
user_constraints: Standard library only; no dependency install, network, shared event file, or v0.1/v0.2 mutation.
permissions: Edit only the two declared new event-log files and use auto-cleaned OS temp directories.
non_goals: Do not build a scheduler, benchmark throughput, or support cross-host clock reconciliation.

acceptance_checks: Record the existing Python 3.10 import failure as RED before changing the UTC implementation.
Use a standard-library UTC expression supported by Python 3.10 without changing serialized timestamps or the public CLI.
Record stable UTC and epoch-nanosecond timestamps in append-only same-owner JSONL.
Reject owner mismatches, unknown events, duplicate transitions, finish-before-start, and incomplete spans.
Classify overlapping and non-overlapping valid intervals exactly and make --require-overlap fail when none overlap.
Run the targeted test module with both local python -B (3.10) and py -3 -B (3.11), reporting versions, exact counts, and exit codes.
